## UDT-011..018 (Filed 2026-07-07, Codex-Maintenance)

- [ ] **[UDT-011]** [Resource Leak] CancellationTokenSource not disposed on replacement in MacroPlayer.cs:63. *Root Cause*: _cancellationTokenSource = new() after CancelAsync() but never .Dispose() 鈥?the old CTS's internal timer/registration resources leak until GC finalizer runs. *Suggested Fix*: ar old = _cancellationTokenSource; _cancellationTokenSource = new(); old?.Dispose();

- [ ] **[UDT-012]** [Resource Leak] CancellationTokenSource not disposed on replacement in FpsSensorController.cs:75. *Root Cause*: _cancellationTokenSource = new CancellationTokenSource() in StartMonitoringAsync() without disposing the prior instance; repeated calls leak CTS objects. *Suggested Fix*: _cancellationTokenSource?.Dispose(); _cancellationTokenSource = new CancellationTokenSource();

- [ ] **[UDT-013]** [Resource Leak] CancellationTokenSource not disposed on replacement in DeviceAutomationPipelineTriggerTabItemContent.xaml.cs:84. *Root Cause*: _filterDebounceCancellationTokenSource = new() after CancelAsync() without disposing the old CTS. Debounce-triggered text changes leak CTS on every keystroke burst. *Suggested Fix*: _filterDebounceCancellationTokenSource?.Dispose(); _filterDebounceCancellationTokenSource = new();

- [ ] **[UDT-014]** [Resource Leak] CancellationTokenSource not disposed on replacement in SpectrumKeyboardBacklightControl.xaml.cs:440,453. *Root Cause*: Two reassignment sites (_refreshStateCancellationTokenSource = new()) cancel-then-replace without disposing the old CTS. Lines 129-135 show the correct dispose pattern is known but not applied at L440/L453. *Suggested Fix*: _refreshStateCancellationTokenSource?.Dispose(); _refreshStateCancellationTokenSource = new();

- [ ] **[UDT-015]** [Threading] GetAwaiter().GetResult() in AIController.Dispose(bool):302 鈥?potential deadlock. *Root Cause*: gameAutoListener.UnsubscribeChangedAsync(...).GetAwaiter().GetResult() blocks the Dispose thread. If the unsubscription requires UI thread (e.g., dispatcher marshal), this deadlocks the finalizer/GC thread. *Suggested Fix*: Fire-and-forget via _ = Task.Run(async () => await gameAutoListener.UnsubscribeChangedAsync(...)) or convert to async dispose (IAsyncDisposable).

- [ ] **[UDT-016]** [Hook Teardown] KB#13 violation in MacroRecorder.cs:89-108 鈥?unhook before field clear. *Root Cause*: PInvoke.UnhookWindowsHookEx(_kbHook) and _mouseHook called while fields still hold the handle; fields cleared only at L110-111 after both unhook calls. If a hook callback fires during unhook, it sees a stale handle. *Suggested Fix*: Capture to local, clear field, then unhook: ar h = _kbHook; _kbHook = default; PInvoke.UnhookWindowsHookEx(h);

- [ ] **[UDT-017]** [Hook Teardown] KB#13 violation in NativeWindowsMessageListener.cs:96-139 鈥?unhook/unregister before field clear. *Root Cause*: UnhookWindowsHookEx(_kbHook) and 4x UnregisterPower* calls precede field clearing at L136+. All handles are still live in fields during teardown, risking stale-handle callback races. *Suggested Fix*: Capture each handle to a local, clear the field to default, then call the unhook/unregister API with the local.

- [ ] **[UDT-018]** [Hook Teardown] KB#13 violation in UserInactivityAutoListener.cs:57-61 鈥?unhook before field clear. *Root Cause*: UnhookWindowsHookEx(_kbHook) and _mouseHook called, then _kbHook = HHOOK.Null; _mouseHook = HHOOK.Null; follows. Same stale-handle race as UDT-016/017. *Suggested Fix*: ar kb = _kbHook; var ms = _mouseHook; _kbHook = default; _mouseHook = default; PInvoke.UnhookWindowsHookEx(kb); PInvoke.UnhookWindowsHookEx(ms);

## New Tickets (pass-2824, 2026-07-07)

- [ ] **[UDT-019]** [Resource Leak] Double Process.GetProcessById without dispose in UniversalDeviceToolkit.Lib/Controllers/Sensors/FpsSensorController.cs:164,169. *Root Cause*: Line 164 creates a using var process for validation, then line 169 creates a SECOND Process object via Process.GetProcessById((int)processId) and returns it to the caller. The returned Process handle leaks to the GC finalizer (no using on the returned object). Additionally, TOCTOU race exists between validation (L166) and second lookup (L169) — process may exit in between. *Suggested Fix*: Return the already-validated process variable from line 164 instead of creating a second lookup: 
eturn IsProcessBlacklisted(process.ProcessName) ? null : process;. This eliminates both the leak and the TOCTOU race.
